h1_route_security_contract.html_shell_boundary: Content-Security-Policy and same-origin static policy are properties of the HTML/static shell only (index.html via _serve_index, csp=True). _send_json() never sets CSP for any JSON route, including /api/state, /api/discover, or the new H1 route; H1 must not claim or invent a CSP response header on its JSON GET.
h1_route_security_contract.human_boundary_law: H1 and its production receipt describe the Chairman or supervised local operator inside the accepted P0A host/account threat boundary -- never an authenticated/authorized human identity, public authorization, or protection from another same-user local process.
h1_route_security_contract.no_partial_write_law: the canonical payload is fully serialized and length-checked before any byte is written to the response; on overflow the fixed route returns WORKROOM_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE instead of a partial body
h1_route_security_contract.post_body_cap_boundary: The existing 64 KiB _MAX_BODY_BYTES cap is enforced only inside _read_json_body(), which is called only from do_POST. The H1 fixed GET route reads no request body, so this cap does not apply to it and must never be described as an H1 GET protection.
